
# Glossary of terms and concepts {.unnumbered}

This chapter is a reference/glossary of various terminology used throughout
this companion, including terminology relating to both the processing of the
Civil Service People Survey data as well as terms and concepts relating more
generally to the operation and management of the Civil Service.

This companion uses the terms 'Civil Service People Survey' and 'People Survey'
interchangeably; the acronym 'CSPS' is used sparingly, usually were space is
at a premium (see the [CSPS entry](#csps) below for further details). 

```{r}
#| echo: false
#| results: asis

# read glossary yaml file
glossary <- yaml12::read_yaml("glossary.yml")

# convert to tibble
glossary_df <- tibble::tibble(glossary) |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    term = purrr::map_chr(.x = glossary, .f = ~.x$term),
    id = purrr::map_chr(
      .x = glossary,
      .f = ~ifelse(is.null(.x$id), NA_character_, .x$id)
      ),
    definition = purrr::map_chr(
      .x = glossary,
      .f = ~ifelse(is.null(.x$definition), NA_character_, .x$definition)
      ),
    refers_to = purrr::map_chr(
      .x = glossary, 
      .f = ~ifelse(is.null(.x$refers_to), NA_character_, .x$refers_to)
      ),
    see_also = purrr::map(
      .x = glossary,
      .f = ~.x$see_also
    ),
    id_all = dplyr::if_else(
      is.na(id),
      gsub("[^A-z0-9]", "-", gsub(",.*", "", tolower(term))),
      id
    ),
    id_all = make.unique(id_all, sep = "-")
  )

refer_terms <- function(refs, df, also = FALSE, locale = "en_GB") {
  
  if (is.null(refs)) {
    return(NA_character_)
  }

  if (length(refs) == 1 && is.na(refs)) {
    return(NA_character_)
  }

  # exclude accidental NAs
  refs <- refs[!is.na(refs)]

  if (length(refs) == 0) {
    return(NA_character_)
  }

  terms_df <- tibble::tibble(
    ref = refs
  ) |>
    dplyr::mutate(
      term = purrr::map_chr(
        .x = ref,
        .f = ~df$term[df$id_all == .x]
      )
    ) |>
    dplyr::arrange(term, .locale = locale)

  term_links <- glue::glue_collapse(
    glue::glue("[{terms_df$term}](#{terms_df$ref})"),
    sep = ", ", last = " and "
  )

  see <- "See "

  if (also) {
    see <- "\n\nSee also: "
  }

  paste0(see, term_links, ".")
  
}

out_df <- glossary_df |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    definition = stringr::str_trim(definition, "right"),
    refer_txt = purrr::map_chr(
      .x = refers_to,
      .f = ~refer_terms(.x, glossary_df)
    ),
    see_also_txt = purrr::map_chr(
      .x = see_also,
      .f = ~refer_terms(.x, glossary_df, TRUE)
    ),
    letter = toupper(substr(term, 1, 1)),
    letter = dplyr::if_else(grepl("\\d", letter), "#", letter),
    # create <dt> tags
    term_tag = paste0("<dt id=\"",id_all,"\">", term,"</dt>"),
    # create <dd> tags
    definition_inner = dplyr::case_when(
      is.na(refer_txt) & is.na(see_also_txt) ~ definition,
      is.na(refer_txt) & !is.na(see_also_txt) ~ paste(definition, see_also_txt),
      !is.na(refer_txt) & is.na(see_also_txt) ~ paste(refer_txt),
      !is.na(refer_txt) & !is.na(see_also_txt) ~ paste(refer_txt, see_also_txt)
    ),
    definition_tag = paste0(
      "<dd>\n",
      definition_inner,
      "\n</dd>"
    )
  ) |>
  dplyr::arrange(tolower(term), .locale = "en_GB") |>
  dplyr::summarise(
    dl_inner = paste0(term_tag, definition_tag, collapse = "\n\n"),
    .by = letter
  ) |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    # create per letter sections and <dl> lists
    output = paste0(
      "## ", letter, "\n",
      "<dl id=\"glossary-", tolower(letter), "\">\n",
      dl_inner,
      "\n</dl>"
    )
  )

# render glossary content
cat(
  paste0(out_df$output, collapse = "\n\n")
)

```
